finding: Regression: tightening this pattern lets a lowercase v1 prefix with a trailing separator pass the no-v1-name rule.
why: 0001 Acceptance requires failing on `afk` not followed by `v2` in storage keys, but `localStorage.setItem("afk_" + key)`, `PREFIX = "afk_"` and `set "P=afk_"` now pass in code files, and `{"prefix": "afk:"}`, `"afk-"` and `"afk/"` now pass in .json/.txt/.md.
fix: Keep the prose carve-out only for `:` and `.` before whitespace: flag `afk[-_]` and `/` or `\` unconditionally, and allow a closing quote after the separator; add these inputs to test_v1_name_in_text_fails.
evidence: Probe evaluated the V1 patterns at HEAD and at d2239c37: `PREFIX = "afk_"` HEAD False, d2239c37 True; `localStorage.setItem("afk_" + key)` HEAD False, d2239c37 True; text-file patterns on `{"prefix": "afk:"}` HEAD False, d2239c37 True. Diff line: `-(?=[-_:./\\a-z0-9])` became `+(?=[-_:./\\][a-z0-9]|[a-z0-9])`.

finding: SUBSTRING_MATCH has no IGNORECASE flag, so the common JS, PowerShell and cmd spellings of prefix and substring matches pass the marker check.
why: 0001 Acceptance says the check fails on code that matches a marker by prefix or substring, but `line.startsWith("afkv2-core-behaviors")` in .js, `$line.StartsWith(...)`, `$line -Match ...`, `select-string ...` in .ps1 and `FINDSTR /c:...` in .cmd all pass, although those suffixes are in CODE_SUFFIXES.
fix: Compile SUBSTRING_MATCH with re.IGNORECASE and add camelCase and uppercase cases to test_prefix_or_substring_marker_match_fails.
evidence: Probe through check_marker_matching: `s.js 'line.startsWith("afkv2-core-behaviors")' False`, `s.js 'line.endsWith(...)' False`, `s.ps1 '$line.StartsWith(...)' False`, `s.ps1 '$line -Match ...' False`, `s.ps1 'select-string -pattern ...' False`, `s.cmd 'FINDSTR /c:...' False`.

finding: The new skip branch lets a hook of any speed end as a skip, not a failure, when the empty .cmd floor is over 50 ms in all five attempts.
why: PRD AC-013 and the 0001 Acceptance bullet both say a slower hook fails; D-9 supersedes only the quoted `## Verification` passage, and root DECISIONS.md says a `Supersedes:` line overrides only the exact passage it quotes, so those two rules still bind. By reading the code, per-attempt medians of (hook 0.500, floor 0.051) reach pytest.skip, and D-9 records load medians up to 81 ms on this machine.
fix: Keep the no-verdict skip only when the hook median minus the floor median stays within a stated margin and fail otherwise, or have the owner rule on an explicit supersession of the AC-013 sentence.
evidence: test_hooks.py:131-132: `if all(floor >= LIMIT_SECONDS for _, floor in attempts):` / `pytest.skip(f"no verdict: an empty .cmd takes over 50 ms on this machine now: {attempts}")`. PRD.md:95: "A slower hook or extra output fails." 0001 Acceptance: "a slower hook or extra output fails the test". D-9: "Supersedes: D-7 in full; 0001 `## Verification` ...".

finding: A v1 name with a leading underscore and no alphanumeric before it passes the rule in code files.
why: The new pattern needs an alphanumeric before `_`, and the bare-word pattern excludes `_` on both sides, so env var `set _AFK=1`, CSS class `._afk {}`, `_afk = 1` and `__afk__` pass; D-10 lists only the bare word in .md/.txt/.json and joined words such as `notafk` as known gaps.
fix: Treat `_` as a boundary, for example `(?<![a-z0-9])_*af[k](?!v2)_*(?![a-z0-9])`, and add these inputs to the tests.
evidence: Probe through check_no_v1_names: `s.py '_afk = 1' False`, `s.py '__afk__' False`, `s.cmd 'set _AFK=1' False`, `s.sh 'export _AFK=1' False`, `s.css '._afk {}' False`. Code line: `(?<=[a-z0-9])[-_]af[k](?![a-z0-9])`.

finding: The new slice-compare rule only sees the slice on the left of the operator, and the operator list misses other partial-match forms.
why: `if "afkv2-core-behaviors" == line[:20]:` is a prefix match that passes, as do `text.rsplit(...)`, `text.rpartition(...)`, `line.removeprefix(...)`, `$line -cmatch ...`, `$line -notmatch ...` and cmd `"%line:~0,20%"=="afkv2-core-behaviors"`.
fix: Also match `[!=]=\s*\w+\[[^\]]*:[^\]]*\]`, add `rsplit`, `rpartition`, `removeprefix`, `removesuffix`, `-[ci]?(?:not)?(?:like|match|contains)` and `%\w+:~`, and test each.
evidence: Probe through check_marker_matching: `s.py 'if "afkv2-core-behaviors" == line[:20]:' False`, `s.py 'text.rsplit(...)' False`, `s.py 'text.rpartition(...)' False`, `s.py 'line.removeprefix(...)' False`, `s.ps1 '$line -cmatch ...' False`, `s.cmd 'if "%line:~0,20%"=="afkv2-core-behaviors" echo y' False`. The positive test covers only `line[:20] == "{MARKER}"`.

finding: A code file that cannot be read passes the check silently, so the gate fails open.
why: `_is_utf8` returns True on OSError and `_text_lines` yields nothing, so a code file holding `afk = 1` that another process holds with no sharing (for example an editor or scanner lock on Windows) gives no problem and the check answers ok.
fix: Report OSError as a problem such as `cannot read`, for example by having the helper return the failure reason, and add a test.
evidence: Probe: with s.py holding `afk = 1`, unlocked `check_no_v1_names` gives `['s.py:1: v1 name: afk = 1']`; after CreateFileW with dwShareMode=0 it gives `locked: [] marker: []`. Code: `except OSError:\n        return True`.

finding: `build` still ends in a traceback with empty stdout when `hooks/built` is a file, because `mkdir` sits outside the new try block.
why: The script's contract is to answer one JSON object, and the delta wraps only write_text, so `plugin_check.py build` with `hooks/built` as a file raises FileExistsError and a caller's json.loads fails on empty stdout.
fix: Move `built.mkdir(...)` inside a try block for OSError that returns a `cannot write` problem, and add a test next to test_prebuilt_path_that_cannot_be_written_answers_json.
evidence: Probe: tree copy with `hooks/built` replaced by a file, `plugin_check.py build` gave returncode 1, stdout `''`, stderr ending `FileExistsError: [WinError 183] Cannot create a file when that file already exists`.

finding: The widened substring-match rule is case-sensitive and misses sibling forms, so common PowerShell, cmd and JS prefix or substring marker matches still pass.
why: 0001 Acceptance says the check fails on code that matches a marker by prefix or substring, and .cmd and .ps1 are in CODE_SUFFIXES with case-insensitive commands; D-4 records only variable data flow as a known gap, and these forms all sit on one line.
fix: Compile SUBSTRING_MATCH with re.IGNORECASE; add `.exec(`, the -c/-i/-not variants of -like/-match/-contains, the cmd `:~` substring form, and a slice on either side of the compare.
evidence: Inline probe of `MARKER_TOKEN.search(t) and SUBSTRING_MATCH.search(t)` with M = afkv2-core-behaviors, all False: 'FINDSTR /c:"M" x'; 'select-string -Pattern "M" x'; '$line.Substring(0,5) -eq "M"'; '$line.StartsWith("M")'; '/M/.exec(line)'; 'if "M" == line[:20]:'; 'if "%L:~0,20%"=="M" echo'; '$l -notmatch "M"'; '$l -cmatch "M"'. The lowercase and left-side forms are True.

finding: The delta narrowed the v1 pattern, and no test case holds a v1 prefix that ends at the separator, so the regression is not caught.
why: Acceptance lists storage keys and `AFK_`; after the narrowing, `"afk_" + name` passes in a .py file, `"afk-"`, `"afk:"` and `"afk."` pass in .txt, .md and .json, and deleting V1_TEXT pattern 0, the only pattern that catches a bare `AFK_` prefix, leaves every listed case flagged.
fix: Add `key = "afk_" + name`, `key = "afk-" + name` and `prefix = "AFK_"` to the failing list, then widen pattern 1 for a quoted prefix while the prose cases stay green.
evidence: plugin_check.py:38 `(?=[-_:./\\][a-z0-9]|[a-z0-9])`. Inline probe with old and new patterns: `key = "afk_" + name` gave V1_TEXT=[] flagged_in_py=False old_pattern1=True; `key = "afk-" + name` gave V1_TEXT=[] flagged_in_txt_json=False old_pattern1=True; `prefix = "AFK_"` gave V1_TEXT=[0]. Enumeration of the 27 listed lines: 0 lines are caught only by pattern 0.

finding: The test takes its suffix cases from the production constant, so deleting a suffix removes its case and the test stays green.
why: D-10 adds .jsx, .tsx, .vue, .html, .css, .yaml, .yml and .toml as a rule, but no test names any of them, so removing `.html` from CODE_SUFFIXES is not detected.
fix: Write the suffix list as a literal in the test, or add one test that asserts CODE_SUFFIXES equals the D-10 set.
evidence: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("suffix", sorted(plugin_check.CODE_SUFFIXES))`. Read of test_plugin_check.py: the other fixed sample names use .py, .cmd, .txt, .md and .png only.

finding: The new slice-compare rule has one sunny case: no case for the reversed operand and no pass-side case, and both directions give a wrong answer.
why: Acceptance says the check fails on a prefix match, but `"marker" == line[:20]` passes; D-4 tells authors to use `==`, but `d["a:b"] == "marker"` is refused.
fix: Add the reversed slice to the failing list and `d["a:b"] == marker` to the passing list, then fix the regex until both hold; also add `awk`, `sls`, `.substring(` and `.substr(`, which no case exercises.
evidence: Probe of MARKER_TOKEN and SUBSTRING_MATCH: `"afkv2-core-behaviors" == line[:20]` gave False; `d["a:b"] == "afkv2-core-behaviors"` gave True. The failing list holds only `line[:20] == ...` for this rule and `sed` from the group `sed|awk|sls`.

finding: The timing gate can still pass by chance and can fail on load alone, because it uses the first passing attempt and absolute limits.
why: A hook near the limit passes if one of five attempts dips under 50 ms, which is the defect D-9 names in D-7; a single floor median under 50 ms beside a loaded hook median also makes the run fail, not skip, although the hook did not change.
fix: Gate on the paired difference of hook minus floor in every attempt, with no pass on the first lucky attempt, and report the absolute median separately.
evidence: `if attempts[-1][0] < LIMIT_SECONDS and attempts[-1][1] < LIMIT_SECONDS: return`. D-9: "the gate is the first median under the limit, so a hook near the limit can pass by chance" and "an empty `.cmd` takes 40 ms to 47 ms", "medians from 41 ms to 81 ms under load". Found by reading; not run.

finding: D-11 understates why the v1 CI job is red, so the two paths it hands to the owner cannot turn CI green.
why: The rule 'at ship, CI must be green' depends on this gap record, but D-11 names only tests.yml and native-contract-allow.txt, and two failure causes cannot be cleared through those paths: gate check K has no allow lookup, and the review-ID test does not read the allow file.
fix: Correct the ledger in a new appended entry that lists every cause (harness-name, plugin-root and project-dir vocabulary, check K on COVERAGE.json, the A2-004 citation in COVERAGE.json), and name a fix path for the investigations folder such as exclusion or redaction.

finding: The no-v1-name scan has no exemption for code that must name v1 artifacts, so planned takeover code can only pass by hiding those names from the check.
why: 0008 must replace a v1 afk:prd block, 0011 must find v1 markers by full line and handle the v1 plugin and config, and 0016 requires plugin_check exit 0 on the merged tree, yet a literal full-line v1 compare fails check_no_v1_names; assembling the name at run time passes, but then check_marker_matching cannot see the v1 marker that 0001 Acceptance line 51 requires it to police.
fix: Have the plan owner choose now: either a narrow, named allow list for v1-takeover constants checked with full-line compare only, or one shared v1-names module the check treats as the sole exception.
evidence: Inline probe with the shipped functions on temp files: 'if line == "<!-- [v1]:prd:start -->":', 'V1_BEGIN = "<!-- [v1]:behaviors:start -->"', 'config = Path(".[v1]") / "config.yaml"', 'switch_off("[v1]")' and 'name = "[v1]@[v1]-toolkit"' (where [v1] is the v1 name) all gave check_no_v1_names=problem and check_marker_matching=pass. _files skips only frozenset({'__pycache__', '.pytest_cache'}). 0008 line 37: 'a v1 afk:prd block is replaced'. 0011 line 38: 'The v1 block is found only by its full begin and end marker lines'. 0016 line 41: 'plugin_check.py exit 0 on the merged tree'. test_plugin_check.py line 16: 'v1 names are assembled at run time so this file itself passes'. No test covers a v1 marker with a full-line compare (test_full_line_marker_match_passes uses the afkv2 MARKER only).

finding: The registration check accepts a non-empty list that holds no handler.
why: `{"SessionStart": [{}]}`, `[1]` and `[{"matcher": "x", "hooks": []}]` give no `no SessionStart registration` problem, although the hook would never run; only test_hooks.py inspects the shape of the shipped file.
fix: Require at least one dict entry whose `hooks` list holds at least one handler with a `command`.
evidence: Probe: the shipped tree with `hooks.SessionStart` set to each value, `run_checks` returned `[]` for `[{}]`, `[1]` and `[{"matcher":"x","hooks":[]}]`. Code: `if not isinstance(registration, list) or not registration:`.

finding: A UTF-16 code file with no BOM passes as UTF-8, and its v1 names are not seen.
why: UTF-16-LE ASCII text is valid UTF-8 with NUL bytes between letters, so `_is_utf8` returns True and no pattern matches `A\0F\0K`; the new test covers only UTF-16 with a BOM.
fix: Treat a code file that holds a NUL character as a `cannot read` problem.
evidence: Probe: `(r/"s.cmd").write_bytes("set AFK_X=1\r\n".encode("utf-16-le"))`, then `check_no_v1_names` gave `[]`.

finding: `_is_utf8` is a drifted twin of the new `_read_text` and the existing `_text_lines`: three wrappers around one read, and each code file is now read twice.
why: The twins disagree on OSError: `_read_text` returns None, but `_is_utf8` returns True and `_text_lines` yields nothing, so an unreadable code file is reported as no problem at all.
fix: Read each file once through one helper that tells 'not UTF-8' from 'unreadable', and have check_no_v1_names report both.
evidence: plugin_check.py:208-215: `except UnicodeDecodeError: return False` / `except OSError: return True`; plugin_check.py:201-205: `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError): return None`; plugin_check.py:95 and :98 call `_is_utf8(path)` and then `_text_lines(path)`, and each calls `path.read_text`.

finding: The usage-error assert compares `reason` with itself, so any value passes, including null or an empty string.
why: The contract answer carries a `reason`, but this assert proves only that the key exists; the same line is at afkv2/tests/test_config.py:171.
fix: Assert the exact key set and `code`, then assert that `reason` is a non-empty string.
evidence: `assert answer == {"ok": False, "error": {"code": "usage", "reason": answer["error"]["reason"]}}`

finding: The no-data-folder test reads machine-wide state at the drive root and checks only that one path, so a record written elsewhere passes.
why: An existing `C:\afkv2` fails the test for a reason unrelated to the hook, and a hook that falls back to a path relative to the current folder still passes a test named `writes_no_record`.
fix: Also assert that `tmp_path / "afkv2"` does not exist, and that no other new file is in `tmp_path`.
evidence: `root_folder = Path(tmp_path.anchor) / "afkv2"` and `assert not root_folder.exists()`. The test has no check under `tmp_path`, while the sibling tests assert `(tmp_path / "afkv2")`.
